memory_update.text: LINC is a direct underfollowed candidate for employer-aligned vocational capacity; prioritize WorkforceLinc conversion, student starts, placement rates, campus expansion, and regulatory risks in Layer 2.
UTI is a direct underfollowed candidate for transportation, skilled-trades, and healthcare technician capacity; verify OEM/manufacturer-specific program economics and active-student growth.
ATGE is a healthcare-workforce capacity analog rather than a skilled-trades pure play; include if the theme branch covers nursing, clinical, and allied-health training bottlenecks.

STRA is a second-order employer-education infrastructure candidate via Workforce Edge and employer-affiliated enrollment; relevance depends on whether employer partnerships include workforce-aligned credentialing beyond generic degree programs.

Need later-layer checks for program-level graduation rates, placement rates, employer hiring outcomes, Title IV/90-10 exposure, cohort default rates, instructor availability, lab/equipment capex, and accreditation constraints.

summary: Layer 1B expanded the universe around employer-recognized vocational capacity rather than broad edtech. The strongest direct small/mid-cap candidates are Lincoln Educational Services and Universal Technical Institute because their operating models map to physical-campus, instructor, lab, equipment, employer-partnership, and placement-capacity constraints. Adtalem is included as a healthcare-workforce capacity analog where clinical education and employer pathways can become bottlenecks. Strategic Education is less directly trades-exposed but is included as a second-order employer-benefits and workforce-education platform with measurable corporate-agreement growth. No trading recommendation is implied.
